final_message:
I've calibrated all seven joint offsets and saved them to `params.json`. The simulated arm now matches the reference photos in all four training poses: fewer than 0.33% of pixels differ, down from 6–7.5% with the default all-zero offsets.

| Parameter | Value (rad) |
|---|---|
| offset_1 | +0.156 |
| offset_2 | −0.178 |
| offset_3 | +0.211 |
| offset_4 | +0.156 |
| offset_5 | −0.240 |
| offset_6 | +0.204 |
| offset_7 | −0.306 |

**How I fit them:** the task is purely kinematic (no dynamics), so I wrote a script (`work/fit.py`) that sets the offsets, renders all 12 views (4 poses × 3 cameras) and scores how far each render is from its reference photo. Each full evaluation took about 0.5 s. I searched in three steps (`work/opt.py`, `work/opt2.py`):
1. A coarse search one joint at a time over the full ±0.4 rad range, on heavily blurred images.
2. A finer search of the same kind on less-blurred images.
3. Two rounds of an automatic optimiser (Powell) on lightly blurred images.

**Results per pose (share of mismatched pixels):**

| Pose | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| pose_0 | 6.3% | 0.30% |
| pose_1 | 7.4% | 0.08% |
| pose_2 | 6.0% | 0.16% |
| pose_3 | 7.5% | 0.33% |

What's left is thin outlines at silhouette edges. The reference photos contain deliberate sensor noise, so a perfect pixel match isn't possible.

**Reliability:** in the last round the offsets moved by less than about 0.005 rad (about 0.3°) and the score barely improved, so they have settled. Joints 1 and 3 partly trade off against each other, and that pair took the longest to settle. Because the four training poses place the arm in very different configurations, the fit should reflect the real joint offsets rather than tuning to these particular photos. I can't score against the held-out poses myself. The pass mark there allows 4° of hand rotation error, far more than the remaining drift.
